# ssp_security_content_bundle (Resource)

Uploads a security-content "mega bundle" archive file to the SSP security content store.

The file is streamed directly from disk in a multipart request rather than buffered fully in memory, so upload memory usage stays roughly constant regardless of file size (bundles can be several GB). After the upload is accepted, the resource polls the bundle's processing status until it reaches a terminal state (`SUCCESS` or `FAILED`), which can take significant time for large bundles.

Corresponds to `POST /ssp/security-content/bundles`, `GET /ssp/security-content/bundles/{bundle-id}`, and `DELETE /ssp/security-content/bundles/{bundle-id}`.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bundle_type` (String) Type of the mega bundle being uploaded. One of `FIREWALL_ATP` (Advanced Threat Protection firewall bundle), `AI_ASSISTANT_FIREWALL` (AI Assistant Firewall bundle), or `AI_ASSISTANT_AVI` (AI Assistant AVI bundle).
- `file_path` (String) Path on local disk to the mega bundle archive file to upload.

### Read-Only

- `bundle_id` (String) Bundle identifier reported by the platform once processed.
- `id` (String) Unique ID of the mega bundle upload.
- `manifest_version` (String) Manifest version of the uploaded bundle.
- `source` (String) Source of the bundle (e.g. `MANUAL_UPLOAD`).
- `ssp_version` (String) SSP product version the bundle was built for.
- `status_message` (String) Human-readable status message accompanying `upload_status`.
- `upload_status` (String) Processing status of the upload (`SUCCESS`, `FAILED`, `RUNNING`, `ACCEPTED`).
